g_policy.reason: The 'if the user declines' field makes replies slower than normal for the rest of the day, so declining leaves the user worse off than before the offer.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 60 minutes of in-app priority routing, not cash or something exchangeable outside the app.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is a return to the profile menu from the Upgrade entry without subscribing; it does not require chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The 'if the user declines' field takes away normal reply speed for the rest of the day. Mechanic m03 supports normal-priority routing as the free baseline, so this removes something free users get today.

g_brand_safety.reason: The placement is a card in the s09 profile menu drawer, which is rated content safe and is away from chats.

c1_revealed_value.reason: The reward samples priority routing, a Janitor+ subscriber benefit shown in s02.e06.

c2_evidence.reason: The existing Upgrade entry and paid priority-routing benefit are supported by s09.e31 and s02.e06; m03 supports the inferred normal-priority free baseline.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward ends after 60 minutes and is capped at two plays per day, rather than granting lasting subscription access. The app already sells the priority-routing advantage in s02.e06.

c5_moment.reason: The trigger occurs when the user returns to the persistent s09 profile menu, a surface the user chooses to open.

c6_fits_simula.reason: The offer is a sponsored game triggered by a detectable menu return; the 'if the ad fails' field says unverified play does not turn on faster replies.

c7_specific.reason: The idea names the s09 Upgrade to Janitor Plus entry and the priority-routing benefit in s02.e06.

other_concern: The proposal describes priority routing as literal queue placement, but the model does not establish how routing is implemented.
